subject: ACME TCO follow-up: token economics, batching levers & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Celine Taylor <ctaylor@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME TCO follow-up: token economics, batching levers & next steps

Hi Celine

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + next steps as promised. I tried to keep this tight so you can share with the team.

Top pain points you shared:
- Production latency spikes during peak search and chat usage (esp. 3-5pm PT).
- Cost unpredictability as usage scales (esp. embeddings for vector search + multi-turn chat).
- Internal policy requires data residency and audit logs for customer conversations.

Goals we discussed:
- Get to a predictable monthly OPEX for inference (target budget: ~$40k/month for Tier-1 traffic).
- Reduce per-query token cost for embeddings-heavy workflows.
- Maintain sub-200ms 95th percentile for short chat queries.

What we covered on cost levers:
- Token economics: modeled per-token costs in the attached TCO spreadsheet (see sheet: "ACME TCO - baseline vs optimized"). We used your avg prompt + response token estimates from today (prompt ~150 tokens, response ~600 tokens for chat; embeddings payloads ~2k tokens/day per user).
- Batching & caching: estimated 18-27% token savings for chat with prefix caching (reused KV cache across sessions) and 22% CPU/GPU savings with request-level batching during your traffic tail windows.
- Model variants: proposed using a quantized 8-bit variant for high-throughput routes and a higher-accuracy float variant for low-volume critical requests. Hybrid routing reduces total cost while preserving quality on priority flows.

Attached: redwood-tco-estimate.xlsx (TCO breakdown) and redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (pricing tiers & reserved capacity options).

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll update the TCO with the cleaned token distributions you said you’d share by Thursday.
2) Rafael will follow up with a draft mutual action plan + procurement checklist.
3) If ok, we can schedule a 30-min tech deep dive for your infra/infraops team next week to validate latency numbers (Marcus can run a targeted perf test).

Can you confirm: is procurement the right loop for the contract stage or should we add someone from legal? Also, is the budget cap of ~$40k/month flexible if we can show incremental ROI from reduced latency/retention?

Thanks

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172
Redwood Inference

From: Celine Taylor <ctaylor@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME TCO follow-up: token economics, batching levers & next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap and the attachments — very helpful. A few quick notes from my side:

- Budget: $40k/month is the current target ceiling for the program owner, but we could stretch to $50k if the ROI on latency/retention is concrete and measured.
- Token estimates look reasonable; I’ll attach a CSV of anonymized token logs by Thursday as discussed (will redline anything sensitive).
- Procurement: yes, procurement@acme.com should be the primary contact for commercial terms. Legal will only need to be looped if there are non-standard clauses.

Next step: please go ahead and incorporate the token logs when I send them. Also we’ll need an estimate for a 12-month reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go — esp. cost delta and commit sizes.

Appreciate it —
Celine
Director, AI Platforms
ACME Corporation

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Celine Taylor <ctaylor@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME TCO follow-up: token economics, batching levers & next steps

Great — thanks Celine. I’ll update the spreadsheet once we get the token CSV. A few clarifications I added into the sheet you already have:

- Reserved vs PAYG: included a model showing 10%, 25%, and 50% commit levels. At ~25% commit we see ~15% unit-cost decrease on generation calls, and ~20% on embeddings due to predictable pooling.
- Bursting: included a monthly burst buffer option for peak hours to protect latency SLOs; pricing shown as a per-hour burst rate in the sheet.
- Break-even ROI: at your current ARR contribution from features using chat & embeddings, we estimate a 6-8 month payback on a $200k annual commitment (model assumptions in the "assumptions" tab).

I’ve also added a recommended technical checklist for Marcus to run during the perf test:
- 95th-percentile latency test at 1k concurrent users (short chat flow)
- Embeddings throughput test with batch sizes 1/4/16 to show diminishing returns
- Validate KV caching on repeated prompts for top 10 intents

Marcus — can you lead the perf test coordination? Rafael, can you start the mutual action plan and add procurement contact? I’ll refresh the TCO and re-share by Thursday EOD.

Best,
Marissa

----
Attachment stub: redwood-tco-estimate.xlsx (updated v2)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Celine Taylor <ctaylor@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual Action Plan & procurement checklist for ACME

Hi ACME procurement team —

Looping you in as discussed. Attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan and procurement checklist to help speed things up on your end. High level timeline:
- Week 1: Finalize scope, token profile & perf test acceptance criteria
- Week 2: Run perf tests & evidence review (SOC/PII controls as needed)
- Week 3: DocuSign & PO issuance

Key items procurement will need from ACME:
- Approved SOW + usage forecast (three-month and twelve-month)
- Key contacts for billing and security questionnaire responses
- Any required redlines (please flag within 3 business days)

Marissa: I’ll prepare a short commercial summary that compares PAYG vs 12-month commit levels (numbers pulled from Marissa's spreadsheet).

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

----
Attachment stub: redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf

Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & procurement checklist for ACME

Thanks Rafael — I shared the usage forecasts and token CSV via the secure link (will email separately). Procurement is copied here and will review the MAP; expect a reply with initial redlines by Monday.

We are tentatively OK to proceed with a 12-month commit if the 25% commit level case (and the 6-8 month payback) holds up after perf validation. Please include the DocuSign envelope link when ready.

Celine
